mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 0.3 percentage points and 100,000 persons respectively within one month signals accelerating labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp AND PAYEMS falls > 100,000 in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises > 0.3pp and PAYEMS falls > 100,000 in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% from the previous month, combined with a concurrent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals a housing-led demand contraction, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls > 10% month-over-month AND GDPC1 falls month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both HOUST and GDPC1 decline in the specified manner.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held at or below 0.25% for more than six months in a low-inflation environment signals prolonged monetary accommodation, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: prolonged monetary accommodation with low inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is at or below 0.25% for over six months and inflation is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months signals reduced household financial buffer and impending consumption cutbacks, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 8 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of eight consecutive months of RSAFS below its 12-month moving average.
